homeSummary: I am a Research Associate in Water Engineering and Management at the Faculty of Civil and Environmental Engineering (FCEE), Asian Institute of Technology (AIT), and a Water Engineering and Management graduate of AIT with 5+ years of research experience in hydrology, geospatial analysis, citizen science, and water resource management — from leading the MESSHI sediment-monitoring project to GIS-based sanitation assessments at GWSC.
biography: I am a Research Associate in Water Engineering and Management at the Faculty of Civil and Environmental Engineering (FCEE), Asian Institute of Technology (AIT), Thailand, and a Water Engineering and Management graduate of AIT, with 5+ years of research experience spanning hydrology, geospatial analysis, citizen science, and water resource management. My work integrates field observations, hydrological and hydraulic modelling, AI/ML, GIS, and remote sensing to address complex water and environmental challenges, and I have contributed to multidisciplinary research projects, peer-reviewed publications, and international conference presentations. Previously, I was a Student Research Assistant at the AIT Global Water & Sanitation Center (GWSC) (June 2025 – April 2026), developing geospatial datasets and ArcGIS/QGIS maps for city-level sanitation assessments across Asia. As Project Leader of the MESSHI Project (2023–2024), I established a suspended sediment laboratory from scratch, deployed real-time sensors in the Himalayas, managed a citizen science team, and co-authored findings presented at AGU and WaterSciCon24. Earlier, as a Research Associate at Smartphones For Water Nepal (5+ years across several roles), I contributed to peer-reviewed publications, managed water quality and streamflow datasets, and represented the organization at international conferences. I am open to research collaborations, academic positions, and water sector opportunities.

researchProjects.title: Citizen Science-based Hydro-meteorological Monitoring of the Kathmandu Valley
researchProjects.description: Focuses on the Kathmandu Valley, where extreme population growth has led to extensive stress and degradation of water resources and associated ecosystems. Mobilizes young researchers and citizen scientists using simple field data collection methods, low-cost sensors, and a standardized, scalable mobile data collection platform to fill data and knowledge gaps in resource- and data-scarce regions while enhancing the quality and applicability of young researchers' efforts. Monitors rainfall, stream and groundwater levels and quality, and freshwater biodiversity, alongside short-term measurement campaigns on monsoon rainfall, land-use change, stone spout flow and quality, streamflow, and stream-aquifer interactions. A one-year project funded by SmartPhones4Water (S4W), continuing a citizen science project (2016–2019) funded by the Swedish International Development Agency (SIDA) and S4W.

researchProjects.title: Monitoring and Evaluating Suspended Sediment in Himalaya (MESSHI)
researchProjects.description: A collaborative initiative between S4W-Nepal and the University of Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA, taking a citizen science approach in which trained citizen scientists collect suspended sediment samples and other data at set intervals, complemented by cost-effective sediment sensors, to provide insight into the sediment dynamics of Nepal's rivers, understand potential impacts on river systems, and support research-based river management strategies. As Project Leader, designed and led project plans, monitoring protocols, and laboratory procedures for suspended sediment analysis; established a fully operational suspended sediment laboratory from scratch and deployed OBS sensors and data loggers at remote Himalayan field sites for real-time turbidity data collection; recruited, trained, and managed a team of citizen scientists and volunteers; and coordinated across international stakeholders, collaborators, and donors. Findings were co-authored and presented at AGU Fall Meeting 2023 and WaterSciCon24, and published in EGUsphere (2026).

researchProjects.title: REAMO — Real-time Asian Meteorological Observatory
researchProjects.description: Aspires to make meteorological data freely available and develop applications throughout (High Mountain) Asia by promoting and developing extensive networks of weather stations from the plains to the mountains. A joint initiative of Utrecht University, S4W-Nepal, ICIMOD, and USOME, building on years of scientific expertise, regional knowledge, and the latest web and weather station technology.

researchProjects.title: VICTORY — Visualizing the Power of Citizen Science Through Observations and Repository for Anticipatory Action
collaborators: Institute of Himalayan Risk Reduction Center (IHRR)
researchProjects.location: Bhimeshwor Municipality, Dolakha & Barbaribiya Municipality, Bardiya, Nepal
researchProjects.description: A collaborative initiative of S4W-Nepal and the Institute of Himalayan Risk Reduction Center (IHRR), funded by the Asian Disaster Preparedness Center (ADPC), implemented over one year in Bhimeshwor Municipality, Dolakha, and Barbaribiya Municipality, Bardiya. Harnesses the collective strength of communities, turning everyday individuals into scientific contributors for an Early Warning System (EWS) for floods and landslides, using low-cost hardware (precipitation and water level sensors) and software solutions (a citizen science crowdsourcing mobile application).

researchProjects.title: Smartphone-Based Urban Flood Modelling
tools: Discharge App (smartphone-based non-contact optical flow measurement)
researchProjects.description: Develops and implements a citizen science-based streamflow monitoring network to address severe urban flooding challenges in the Kathmandu Valley. Operationalizes the smartphone-based Discharge app to generate high-resolution time-series streamflow data, overcoming the limitations of traditional measurement techniques through non-contact optical flow measurement of streams. Carried out in collaboration with Photrack AG.

researchProjects.title: Multi-Hazard Climate Risk Assessment of Road Infrastructure, Cambodia
researchProjects.institution: Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB), under Dr. Srinivasan Ancha
researchProjects.description: Conducted a comprehensive climate risk assessment of road infrastructure across 10 provinces in Cambodia, supporting AIIB-funded climate resilience and infrastructure planning initiatives. Developed high-resolution multi-hazard risk maps for 38 priority road segments using advanced GIS and spatial analysis techniques. Assessed five major climate hazards — flood, drought, landslide, heatwave, and coastal flooding — to evaluate both current and future risk. Generated clear, decision-ready visualizations and maps to communicate complex climate risks to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
